prompt:
Find real, published measurements of how much battery life a typical Bluetooth LE smart home sensor (e.g. Zigbee or BLE door/temperature sensors) actually achieves in the field, as opposed to manufacturer claims. Cite the sources and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
## Field-measured battery life for Zigbee/BLE smart home sensors

I found several sources with real-world measurements spanning multiple years of use, as well as controlled benchmarks. Here are the sourced claims:

---

SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Motion sensor 1 (RTCGQ01LM) : sits on the landing and of an evening, turns on nightlights for a period of time and then if no further motion detected after a couple of minutes, turns the lights back off. This is used all day every day, several times a day. Battery life: 36%" | CLAIM: A heavily-used Aqara Zigbee motion sensor on CR2032 retained 36% battery after 2 full years of daily multi-trigger use, suggesting roughly 3+ year real-world battery life even under heavy trigger frequency.

SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Motion sensor 2 (RTCGQ01LM): sits in a cupboard and turns on additional lighting when the cupboard doors are open, and again, if no further motion detected turns the lights back off. Used rarely, couple of times a week if that. Battery life: 100%" | CLAIM: An infrequently-triggered Aqara Zigbee motion sensor showed 100% battery after 2 years, demonstrating that trigger frequency is the dominant variable in battery drain.

SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Office- Battery life: 37% … Bedroom- Battery life: 45%" | CLAIM: Aqara Zigbee temperature/humidity/pressure sensors (WSDCGQ11LM, CR2032) dropped to 37–45% after 2 years, implying roughly 4-year total battery life for always-on environmental sensors.

SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Door opened a couple of times a month on average (more in summer obviously). Battery life: 100%" | CLAIM: An Aqara Zigbee contact sensor (MCCGQ11LM) still showed 100% battery after 2 years of occasional use, showing contact sensors can far exceed manufacturer claims when triggers are rare.

SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "The battery life on these sensors has been nothing short of brilliant. Obviously the environmental sensors are going to be the ones dropping the fastest, but the batteries are an easy replacement when they do run out eventually." | CLAIM: The author's overall assessment after 2 years: environmental (temperature/humidity) sensors drain fastest, but all Aqara Zigbee sensors outperformed expectations.

SOURCE: https://asidehouse.com/gizmo/a-year-with-aqara-motion-sensors-dotted-round-the-house/ | QUOTE: "Aqara rates these sensors for roughly a year of battery life on their CR2450 coin cell, and across seven units placed in genuinely different conditions, the real figure has run ahead of that estimate for six of the seven." | CLAIM: In a 12-month real-world test of seven Aqara motion sensors, six of seven exceeded the manufacturer's claimed ~1-year battery life.

SOURCE: https://asidehouse.com/gizmo/a-year-with-aqara-motion-sensors-dotted-round-the-house/ | QUOTE: "The two bathroom sensors, which trigger dozens of times a day given how often that space is used, are the closest to needing a swap at the twelve-month mark, currently reporting under 20% in the app." | CLAIM: High-frequency motion sensors (dozens of triggers/day) fell below 20% battery at 12 months, consistent with the ~1-year manufacturer rating.

SOURCE: https://asidehouse.com/gizmo/a-year-with-aqara-motion-sensors-dotted-round-the-house/ | QUOTE: "The garage sensor, triggered only a handful of times a week, still shows over 70% remaining." | CLAIM: A lightly-triggered Aqara motion sensor retained >70% after a full year, suggesting 3+ year battery life for low-activity locations.

SOURCE: https://asidehouse.com/gizmo/a-year-with-aqara-motion-sensors-dotted-round-the-house/ | QUOTE: "battery life on this category scales with trigger frequency far" | CLAIM: The author's key finding: real-world battery life varies enormously by trigger frequency, making any single manufacturer figure unreliable as a universal claim.

SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "All sensors used fresh CR2032 coin cells (225mAh capacity), reported door/window state every 30 seconds, and logged voltage every 10 minutes. End of life was defined as voltage dropping below 2.0V (sensor shutdown). Test duration: 12 months, all 120 sensors completed the test with no hardware failures." | CLAIM: A controlled 12-month benchmark of 120 sensors (40 each Zigbee 3.0, Z-Wave 800, Wi-Fi 6) on CR2032 cells, reporting every 30 seconds, with voltage-based end-of-life detection.

SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "| 30 seconds | 14.3 | 18.2 | 4.3 |" | CLAIM: At 30-second reporting intervals, measured battery life was 14.3 months (Zigbee 3.0), 18.2 months (Z-Wave 800), and only 4.3 months (Wi-Fi 6) on CR2032.

SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "| 60 seconds | 22.7 | 28.5 | 7.1 |" | CLAIM: Halving reporting to 60 seconds roughly doubled measured battery life: 22.7 months (Zigbee), 28.5 months (Z-Wave), 7.1 months (Wi-Fi).

SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "Zigbee 3.0 battery life dropped by 18% (14.3 to 11.7 months) due to retransmissions, Z-Wave 800 saw no drop (18.2 months) as 908MHz is unaffected by 2.4GHz interference" | CLAIM: Under heavy 2.4 GHz interference, measured Zigbee battery life dropped 18% (to 11.7 months) due to retransmissions, while Z-Wave was unaffected.

SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "For industrial environments with heavy 2.4GHz interference (e.g., factories with 50+ Wi-Fi devices), Zigbee battery life dropped to 8.1 months, while Z-Wave remained at 17.9 months." | CLAIM: In extreme 2.4 GHz noise, measured Zigbee battery life fell to 8.1 months—nearly half the clean-environment figure—showing environment matters as much as protocol.

SOURCE: https://smarthomescene.com/reviews/best-selling-zigbee-temperature-sensors-tested/ | QUOTE: "outside of this test, I've been running first-gen Aqara sensors in my own home for years without a battery change. They are among the most efficient Zigbee temperature and humidity sensors out there, even though they run on a single CR2032 battery." | CLAIM: A reviewer running first-gen Aqara Zigbee temperature sensors reports multiple years without a battery swap on a single CR2032, corroborating thesmarthomebook's 2-year data.

SOURCE: https://smarthomescene.com/reviews/best-selling-zigbee-temperature-sensors-tested/ | QUOTE: "Paulie ● deserves a specific mention here too. Its CR2477 packs meaningfully more capacity than a standard CR2032, at the cost of just a bit of extra thickness. Its official rated battery life is 4 years, the best in this comparison." | CLAIM: The SONOFF SNZB-02P Zigbee temperature sensor carries a 4-year official battery rating (CR2477), though the reviewer notes they did not independently verify this in the test.

SOURCE: https://www.cnx-software.com/2024/04/29/review-sonoff-snzb-06p-zigbee-human-presence-snzb-04pdoor-window-sensor/ | QUOTE: "SONOFF claims up to 5 years, but we know it really depends on usage." | CLAIM: SONOFF claims 5-year battery life for the SNZB-04P Zigbee door sensor, but the reviewer cautions that real-world results depend heavily on usage patterns.

---

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A long-term (multi-year) real-world battery study specifically for Bluetooth LE (BLE) smart home sensors (e.g., Xiaomi Mijia BLE, Govee BLE, SwitchBot BLE) with measured remaining capacity over time. All field data found was for Zigbee sensors; BLE sensor longevity data is only available via manufacturer claims or very short-term reviews.
